dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Today we're talking about stereotypes. Can anyone tell me a stereotype about a country?
dialogue.reading: təˈdeɪ wɪr ˈtɔːkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ˈstɛriətaɪps. kən ˈɛniwʌn ˈtɛl miː ə ˈstɛriətaɪp əˈbaʊt ə ˈkʌntri?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: People say the British drink tea all day!
dialogue.reading: ˈpiːpəl ˈseɪ ðə ˈbrɪtɪʃ ˈdrɪŋk ˈtiː ˈɔːl ˈdeɪ!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: And people say the Japanese are always on time.
dialogue.reading: ənd ˈpiːpəl ˈseɪ ðə ˌdʒæpəˈniːz ər ˈɔːlweɪz ɑːn ˈtaɪm.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Good. What about the Thai? What do foreigners say about Thai people?
dialogue.reading: ˈɡʊd. ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ðə ˈtaɪ? ˈwʌt duː ˈfɔːrənərz ˈseɪ əˈbaʊt ˈtaɪ ˈpiːpəl?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Not really. My parents are never late!
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːt ˈriːli. maɪ ˈpɛrənts ər ˈnɛvər ˈleɪt!

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: That's the problem with stereotypes. Every society has many different people.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ðə ˈprɑːbləm wɪð ˈstɛriətaɪps. ˈɛvri səˈsaɪəti ˈhæz ˈmɛni ˈdɪfərənt ˈpiːpəl.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: But cultures have different values. Respect for older people is important in Thai culture.
dialogue.reading: bʌt ˈkʌltʃərz ˈhæv ˈdɪfərənt ˈvæljuːz. rɪˈspɛkt fər ˈoʊldər ˈpiːpəl ɪz ɪmˈpɔːrtənt ɪn ˈtaɪ ˈkʌltʃər.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Right. Values are part of a culture, but a stereotype is too simple.
dialogue.reading: ˈraɪt. ˈvæljuːz ər ˈpɑːrt əv ə ˈkʌltʃər, bʌt ə ˈstɛriətaɪp ɪz ˈtuː ˈsɪmpəl.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: So when we meet foreigners, we should see the person, not the stereotype.
dialogue.reading: soʊ wɛn wiː ˈmiːt ˈfɔːrənərz, wiː ʃʊd ˈsiː ðə ˈpɜːrsən, ˈnɑːt ðə ˈstɛriətaɪp.
